fable.w: The tempting reading is that the 30-day advance notice requirement is a consultation step before a federal decision. But the only parties notified are the congressional intelligence committees, which are inside the federal government, so this is intra-government notification. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is given any role in the reprogramming decision.
fable.s: unless the congressional intelligence committees are notified 30 days in advance of such reprogramming of funds

qwen_block.w: The section requires notification to the congressional intelligence committees. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, coordination or notification with Congress does not constitute participation with outside parties.
qwen_block.s: unless the congressional intelligence committees are notified 30 days in advance of such reprogramming of funds

opus.w: The only procedural requirement is advance notice to the congressional intelligence committees before funds are reprogrammed or transferred. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so this is coordination within the government, not participation. Nothing here brings in states, experts, the public, or any other outside party, and it grants no right to sue or object.
opus.s: unless the congressional intelligence committees are notified 30 days in advance of such reprogramming of funds
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this counts as participation, because the reprogramming can't happen until someone has been given 30 days' advance notice. That fails here: the only party notified is "the congressional intelligence committees," and Congress is inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public takes part in the decision.

qwen_chat.s: unless the congressional intelligence committees are notified 30 days in advance of such reprogramming of funds
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying congressional committees constitutes "participation" because it involves a formal procedural step before a decision (reprogramming funds) is finalized. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, notification to Congress is intra-governmental coordination/reporting, not participation by an outside party.
